claim.pdf_says:
MERGE general format (14.9.24.2), final group is a single tall BRACE spanning two lines:
{ OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS procedure-name-1 [ { THROUGH } procedure-name-2 ]
{                                        { THRU    }
{ GIVING { file-name-4 } ...
claim.markdown_says:
[ OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS procedure-name-1 [ { THROUGH } procedure-name-2 ] ]
[                                         { THRU    }                    ]
[ GIVING { file-name-4 } ...                                             ]
claim.why_it_matters: The PDF uses a brace, which per 5.2.6.2 means exactly one of the enclosed alternatives is REQUIRED: every MERGE statement shall specify either an OUTPUT PROCEDURE or a GIVING phrase. The markdown replaces the one brace with two independent brackets, which says both are optional and both may be omitted or both given. That both weakens a mandatory requirement (a MERGE with neither phrase would be accepted) and permits an illegal combination (OUTPUT PROCEDURE together with GIVING).

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct glyph inspection at 300 dpi, plus a 2x crop of the final group and a 3x crop of the left edges of the two adjacent groups (E:/Temp/specrecon/v687/final_group.png, left_edges.png).

WHAT I SEE IN THE PDF. The MERGE general format on page 687 (printed page 657) has three multi-line delimited groups. Group 2 (COLLATING SEQUENCE) is drawn with a SQUARE BRACKET: right-angle corners top and bottom, a straight vertical spine, no midpoint feature. Group 3 (OUTPUT PROCEDURE / GIVING) is drawn with a CURLY BRACE: curled hooks at top and bottom and an unmistakable middle cusp pointing left at the vertical midpoint between the OUTPUT PROCEDURE line and the GIVING line, with the mirrored '}' on the right. Side by side in left_edges.png the two shapes are plainly different families. The PDF glyph is a brace; the claim quotes the PDF correctly.

WHAT THE MARKDOWN SAYS. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 28280-28282 are quoted verbatim in the claim (no misquote). The outer delimiter is ASCII '[' at column 0 on all three lines with the closing ']' at columns 72/73/73 - i.e. a tall BRACKET drawn by repeating the glyph per line, the same convention this very code block uses for the tall inner brace of the COLLATING group at lines 28274-28276.

WHY IT IS NOT FORMATTING. 5.2.6.2 (Brackets): the enclosed portion 'may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted.' 5.2.6.3 (Braces): the enclosed portion 'shall be explicitly specified or is implicitly selected.' Bracket vs brace is exactly the required/optional distinction, so the substitution changes normative meaning, not appearance.

NO RESCUE ELSEWHERE. MERGE syntax rules 1-13 (pages 687-688, md lines 28288-28333) never state that one of OUTPUT PROCEDURE / GIVING shall be present; rules 11 and 12 only say 'if the GIVING phrase is specified'. The format diagram's brace is the sole normative carrier of the requirement, so losing it loses the requirement outright.

SIBLING PROOF IN THE SAME DOCUMENT. The SORT statement Format 1 (md lines 31467-31471, page 775) transcribes the structurally identical OUTPUT PROCEDURE / GIVING group with real Unicode brace glyphs U+23A7/U+23A8/U+23A9 and U+23AB/U+23AC/U+23AD. The high-fidelity transcription of the same construct elsewhere confirms the intended glyph and marks page 687 as the defective one.

One part of the claim's rationale is overstated - see corrected_description.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, with the rationale narrowed. Confirmed defect: in the MERGE general format (14.9.24.2, md lines 28280-28282), the tall CURLY BRACE that the PDF prints around the two mutually exclusive alternatives 'OUTPUT PROCEDURE IS procedure-name-1 [{THROUGH|THRU} procedure-name-2]' and 'GIVING {file-name-4}...' is transcribed as a tall SQUARE BRACKET. Per 5.2.6.3 the brace makes selection of one alternative mandatory; per 5.2.6.2 the bracket makes the whole group omissible. The transcription therefore permits a MERGE with neither an OUTPUT PROCEDURE nor a GIVING phrase, which the standard forbids, and no MERGE syntax rule (1-13) restores the requirement.

Correction to the claim's wording: the claim describes the markdown as 'two independent brackets' permitting OUTPUT PROCEDURE together with GIVING. The markdown actually repeats '[' at column 0 on all THREE lines with ']' near-aligned at columns 72/73/73 - the same per-line tall-delimiter convention used for the inner brace of the COLLATING group two lines above - so the natural reading is ONE tall bracket spanning the group, i.e. at-most-one, not both. The certain and unambiguous defect is required-choice degraded to optional. The 'both phrases permitted' consequence is only a secondary risk if a consumer reads the three '[...]' pairs as independent; it should not be asserted as the primary harm.

Suggested fix: redraw the group with the Unicode brace glyphs already used for the identical SORT Format 1 group at md lines 31467-31471 (U+23A7/23A8/23A9 and U+23AB/23AC/23AD), and add a figure note recording that per 5.2.6.3 exactly one of OUTPUT PROCEDURE / GIVING shall be specified and that the THROUGH/THRU bracket attaches only to the OUTPUT PROCEDURE alternative. Consider sweeping the whole file for other ASCII-bracket renderings of tall braces in general formats - this is a pattern, not a one-off.
